title: Role surface mapping, resource graph, and explicit-deny strategy for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Define a production-ready role model for RBAC v2 that is explicit, query-efficient, and compatible with SSO/SAML group mappings and audit logging. The design must cover: a) a resource graph model (nodes: org, tenant, project, dataset, model, endpoint) with fine-grained scopes; b) role surface definition (capabilities/verbs and allowed resource scopes); c) explicit-deny precedence and conflict resolution rules; d) performance/caching strategy for authorization checks at scale; e) a migration path from RBAC v1 to v2 that preserves current admin flows and audit trails.

Key constraints and non-goals: this ticket focuses on the role model and runtime authorization semantics. It does not include UI wiring for role editing or SSO provider onboarding integration code (those are separate tickets). We avoid introducing per-request permission evaluation that requires multiple DB round-trips. The model should allow efficient evaluation from a compiled role catalog and a cached principal-role binding index.

Design decisions summary: 1) Resource graph instead of flat resource paths to enable expressive multi-parent resources (e.g., endpoint belongs to model and project). 2) Scope tokens use canonical tuples (resource_type:action:resource_scope) to keep permission checks constant-time once role expansion is cached. 3) Explicit deny is stronger than allow; deny rules are attached to role bindings and to tenant-level policy; deny winning is essential for break-glass and legal hold scenarios. 4) Role bindings can be tenant-scoped or org-scoped; bindings support temporal windows for temporary elevation. 5) SAML/group mappings will materialize into principal bindings during sync and create shadow bindings with source metadata for audit.

Trade-offs considered: - Normalizing roles into a compact permission bitset gives fast checks but is less human readable; we will store both an authoritative structured representation and a serialized bitset for fast evaluation. - Eagerly expanding inherited permissions at bind-time increases write cost but reduces read latency. We'll use hybrid approach: eager expansion for tenant-admin and global-admin roles; lazy expansion plus caching for large user-group mappings. - Explicit deny simplifies safety but complicates exception workflows; we'll require an "override" break-glass flow that creates time-limited admin bindings with strong audit requirements.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Documented resource graph schema with node types and allowed parent relationships (org -> tenant -> project -> {dataset, model, endpoint}).
A2: Role schema defined (name, description, permission tuples, deny tuples, metadata, temporal window).
A3: Authorization evaluation algorithm pseudo-code that handles allow/deny resolution, precedence, and caching.
A4: Example permission matrix for 8 canonical roles (viewer, editor, deployer, model-admin, tenant-admin, org-admin, billing, support-agent) mapping to actions on each resource type.
A5: Migration plan that includes DB schema changes, a backfill strategy, a rollout plan with feature flag gating, and an audit log retention plan.
A6: Performance targets: median auth check < 3ms in hot cache, 95th percentile < 12ms with group-boundaries; fallback uncached checks documented with expected costs.
A7: Security review sign-off and Confluence design link provided.
A8: Integration notes for SSO/SAML: group-to-role sync spec and conflict handling documented.
A9: Unit tests and an integration test harness that simulates role conflicts and deny-win scenarios.
A10: Monitoring metrics defined (auth_check_latency, auth_cache_hit_rate, deny_rate_by_tenant) and dashboards proposed in Console.
notes: Resource graph will be implemented as adjacency table (resource_id, parent_id, type) with precomputed path tokens for fast matching.
Permission tuples will be stored as canonical strings (e.g., 'model:deploy:project-123') and indexed by permission hash for quick lookup.
We will introduce a compact permission bitmap column for runtime serverside checks; the bitmap is derived from the authoritative permission set at bind-time.
Deny semantics: deny entries are stored alongside allow entries with a deny_flag; evaluation short-circuits on first matching deny in binding precedence order.
Cache strategy: LRU cache at service edge keyed by (principal_id, resource_path_hash, action) with TTL 60s, invalidated on role-binding changes via pub/sub.
Telemetry: add traces to auth path to attribute time to expansion, DB read, cache, and policy evaluation for SLO debugging.
DB migration considerations: avoid long locks; add new tables/columns behind a feature flag and backfill in small batches with progress checkpoints.
Design doc location: Confluence (doc link in references).

2025-02-10 | Priya Mehta (PM): Confirmed canonical role list; requested explicit support for temporary elevation and audit trail requirements from compliance team.

2025-02-18 | Design review (internal): Feedback from infra: ensure pub/sub invalidation scale for >100k binding changes/day. Suggest sharded invalidation keys. Action: incorporate sharded channel names and backoff on rebuild.

2025-02-22 | Mark Chen: Prototype PR submitted for resource graph storage and path resolution (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821). Requesting review from data-modeling and infra leads.

2025-02-27 | QA: Added auth tests that simulate group sync churn and deny conflicts. Found a race where a newly-applied deny binding was not visible to requests in-flight; mitigation: short TTL and immediate invalidation event on deny writes. Added to migration checklist.

migration_plan: Step 1: Create new tables (resource_graph, role_catalog_v2, role_bindings_v2, permission_bitmaps) behind feature flag.
Step 2: Backfill role_catalog_v2 by translating v1 roles into v2 tuples; create bitmaps for tenant-admin and org-admin eagerly.
Step 3: Run group-sync process to materialize SSO mappings into role_bindings_v2 in batches of 5k users with progress checkpoints.
Step 4: Enable auth-service dual-read mode: consult v2 first, fallback to v1 if v2 binding not found; log mismatches for 48h.
Step 5: Flip feature flag to v2-only for a pilot tenant; monitor auth metrics, audit logs, and fallback counts.
Step 6: Full rollout with staged enablement and final deprecation of v1 tables after 30 days of stable metrics.
Rollback plan: re-enable dual-read and revert feature flag, replay v1 writes where necessary, and notify customers via Console messages.
